speaker: Doctor
text: I have received your report of grunting, intercostal and subcostal retractions, and peripheral cyanosis; these are classic signs of severe respiratory distress. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray and Arterial_Blood_Gas. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: pH: 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2: 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2: 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3-: 24 mEq/L; Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood gas confirms respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, and the chest X-ray showing fine reticular granularity and ground-glass appearance in a newborn with grunting and retractions is highly suggestive of Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn (PPHN). DIAGNOSIS READY: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn (PPHN).
